Notes: First mention of Zhovkva's Jews dates to 1593; by 1601 a Jewish street existed
Founder Stanislaw Zolkiewski allowed Jews (mostly former Lviv residents) to settle and build a prayer house; Jewish community independent in 1626; first synagogue 1626
Jews formed an organized community and could build synagogue and mikveh and cemetery (per Ukrainian local-history article)
Jews occupied 21 buildings (house count; no population figure)
Jews occupied 88 buildings (house count; no population figure)
Jewish community numbered over 1500 persons and owned over 270 buildings ('over 1500', minimum)
At the beginning of the German occupation Jews numbered around 4500 and were almost half the town's population (approximate)
Approximately 3200 of over 5000 Zhovkva Jews were sent to Belzec by Nov 1942 (deportation count; remaining population figure not used)
Ghetto liquidated 25 Nov 1943; over 4000 shot in Bir forest, others sent to Janowska/Rawa-Ruska, none returned; Jews destroyed as a community
About 70 Jews remained when Soviet forces arrived 23 July 1944 (survivors who hid in bunkers or were rescued; survivor count)
